PowerPoint slides with officer

Source: R/office.R
phw_pptx.Rd

phw_pptx() starts a PowerPoint deck, from the PHW template (16:9, Ubuntu text, navy titles) or from your own. phw_add_slide() adds a slide with a PHW-styled title and a chart, table or text, so a set of results becomes a deck in a few lines. Charts are added as editable vector graphics when the rvg package is installed, so colleagues can tweak them in PowerPoint.

Usage

phw_pptx(template = NULL)

phw_add_slide(
  x,
  title = NULL,
  plot = NULL,
  table = NULL,
  text = NULL,
  source = NULL,
  date = NULL,
  layout = "Title and Content",
  master = NULL,
  editable = TRUE,
  title_size = 28,
  caption_args = list(),
  alt = NULL,
  plot_scale = 1.5,
  table_fit = TRUE,
  continued = NULL
)

Arguments

template

Path to a .pptx template, e.g. the PHW corporate template. NULL uses the PHW template from phw_reference_pptx().

x

An rpptx object from phw_pptx().

title

Slide title, a single string.

plot

A ggplot, or a grob or gtable such as a phw_finalise() result. A grob goes on the slide as a picture.

table

A data frame, flextable or summary table (rendered with phw_flextable()). A table with no rows, such as one a filter left empty, goes on one slide with its header row. A flextable's caption, such as the one phw_flextable() adds, goes in a row at the top of the table, because PowerPoint does not show table captions. Text in the table is never smaller than 12 pt, so it can be read when projected. A table too long for the slide tightens its row spacing, and if it still does not fit, its rows continue on further slides with the same title. Each of them repeats the table's header row and marks its caption, or the title if the table has none, with continued. Any other content goes on the first of them, and the source on the last.

text

Character vector of bullet points. On a title slide or section header it is plain lines in the template's own colour and size.

source, date

Passed to phw_caption() and shown at the bottom, in white on a dark slide background and in the PHW text colour otherwise.

layout, master

Slide layout and slide master names in the template. A slide master is the set of layouts a template provides; see them in PowerPoint under View > Slide Master, or with officer::layout_summary(x). The default master = NULL uses the master in the deck that has the layout (the first one, if several do), so you only need master when two masters share a layout name.

Give one of plot, table or text for each content area. The PHW template has these layouts:

  • "Title and Content" (the default): one chart, table or text.

  • "Two Content": two side by side. With one, it goes on the left. With two, the first of plot, table and text goes on the left.

  • "Comparison": two side by side, under a heading on each side. The headings stay empty for you to fill in.

  • "Content with Caption": one chart, table or text on the right, with a narrow text box on the left that stays empty for you to fill in.

  • "Title Only": one chart, table or text in the space below the title.

  • "Blank": one chart, table or text filling the slide. It has no title.

  • "Title Slide" and "Section Header": a title and text on navy. They have no room for a chart or table.

With your own template, give the layout names it uses.

editable

Add charts as editable vector graphics (needs rvg)?

title_size

Title font size. On a title slide or section header the template sets the size and colour, and this applies only when you give it.

caption_args

List of other phw_caption() arguments.

alt

Alternative text for the chart or table on the slide, read out by screen readers. NULL adds none, except that a ggplot's own labs(alt = ) text is used when there is one. On a slide with two contents, it goes on the first.

plot_scale

How much to enlarge a chart's text on the slide, as a multiple of the size the chart already uses. The default 1.5 brings axis and legend text to about 14 points, which reads from the back of a room. 1 leaves the chart as it is. It scales the text and legend keys that follow the plot's base size, as theme_phw() and the ggplot2 themes do, and the size of text drawn by geom_text() with ggplot2 4.0.0 or later. Text you gave an exact size in your own theme() keeps it. A grob keeps the sizes it was drawn with.

table_fit

Enlarge a table built here from a data frame or summary table, or made with phw_flextable(), so it fills the slide's content area? Its text grows from 12 pt up to 18 pt, as far as the area has room, and its columns widen with it. A narrow table is then widened by at most another 80% (more for a table with more columns), never past the area. A table that continues on further slides grows only as far as it can without taking more slides, and shows the same size on each. FALSE keeps the text at 12 pt. A flextable you made with flextable::flextable() is never enlarged. Either way, a table too wide for the area wraps its headings, then its cells, and one still too wide gives a warning. The text never shrinks below 12 pt.

continued

Text added after the caption, or after the title if the table has no caption, on the slides a long table continues on. NULL uses the continued text of a phw_flextable(), or "(continued)". Give your own wording, for example in Welsh.

Value

An officer rpptx object. Save it with print(deck, target = "file.pptx").

Details

Every argument is checked before the slide is added, so a call that stops leaves the deck as it was.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("officer", quietly = TRUE)) {
  deck <- phw_pptx()
  deck <- phw_add_slide(deck, "Key messages",
                        text = c("Point one", "Point two"))
  if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
    p <- ggplot2::ggplot(mtcars, ggplot2::aes(wt, mpg)) + ggplot2::geom_point()
    deck <- phw_add_slide(deck, "A chart", plot = p, source = "mtcars", editable = FALSE)
    deck <- phw_add_slide(deck, "A chart and its data", plot = p,
                          table = head(mtcars[, c("wt", "mpg")]),
                          layout = "Two Content", editable = FALSE)
  }
  print(deck, target = tempfile(fileext = ".pptx"))
}
